For press

For press

A factual description, key facts that can be checked, and where to find the public record.

What it is

Triarchal Democracy is a proposed model of community governance. It combines one Member, one vote on every binding decision; delegation that is public, revocable at any instant and expires unless renewed; a public, permanent contribution record; and a two-tier dividend that is gated and not live. The Triarc is the project testing the model by governing itself with it, in public. It is not yet incorporated. Triarchal Framework is the open-source software the Triarc runs on.

The Triarc says its primary output is evidence, including failures: it intends to publish measures such as delegation-renewal rates, Dispute Panel outcomes and treasury arithmetic on a fixed cadence. (About The Triarc) Its founding documents are first drafts, offered as proposals and not as ratified law, and are written to be challenged. The project does not name or profile any individual; that is deliberate.

Key facts

Checkable against the published documents and software

  • Eleven founding documents: the Founding Charter and ten codes and compacts. All are proposals, not ratified law.
  • One Member, one vote. Votes and standing cannot be bought, sold, inherited or transferred. Amending that protection needs three quarters of votes cast with at least 40% of Members taking part. (Charter 1.2, 8.2)
  • Delegation is public and revocable at any instant, and by default expires after a year unless renewed, or after 90 days for critical decisions. (Charter 3.3)
  • Minimum age is 18, by declaration; there is no age check. Every verified Member is entitled to the dividend, with no separate age condition. (Charter 1.1; Treasury Code 9.1)
  • The dividend is gated and nothing has been paid. Both tiers stay blocked until a deployment has 30 verified Members and every Delegate Position it has defined is filled. (Treasury Code 5.1)
  • The founder holds temporary powers that end on measured criteria computed from the public record, and the community can end them at any time by a two-thirds vote. (Charter Article IX)
  • Identity and the record are at "Stage 1". That means conventional authentication and append-only by application convention, "not yet by cryptography". (Charter 1.5, 7.1)
  • No tokens and no cryptocurrency. Treasury funds would be held in ordinary currency through regulated institutions, and the Triarc uses no tokens, smart contracts or on-chain voting. (Treasury Code 6.4; About The Triarc)
  • The software is licensed AGPL-3.0, its source is public at github.com/triarchal-democracy/triarchal-democracy, and it runs on Cloudflare Workers with a D1 database. A live deployment is at triarchalframework.triarchal-democracy.workers.dev.
  • One public deployment exists, the Triarc, and no government has adopted or recognised it. (Federation Compact, status note; Government Adoption Compact 2.1)
  • The Triarc is not yet incorporated. The plan is federal incorporation under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act. (About The Triarc)
Please be careful with
  • Income. No dividend has been paid, and the Treasury Code says the amount is "never fixed or promised in advance". The arithmetic page is a costing model of a full adoption that has not happened, not a forecast.
  • Government involvement. The documents describe a staged path that starts with an opt-in network needing nobody's permission. None of the later stages has begun.
  • "Live". The platform works, but several parts are not built or not yet exercised, such as the disputes system, notifications and the dividend. The candid list is on Known limits.
